executiveSummary:
Actuals are reported through December 2025; all periods from January 2026 onward are forecast. Based on actuals, the business reached £9.4M ARR with 70% growth over the last year, 78% gross margin, and a Rule of 40 at 63. Efficiency remains attractive (CAC ratio ~0.56, LTV/CAC 6.5), but retention weakened (gross 79%, logo 85%, net 90%), and Q4’25 ARR net additions slowed materially as new logos fell and churn ticked up. EBIT improved quarter-on-quarter but remained slightly negative in Q4’25.

The forecast assumes a return to faster ARR expansion, improved logo retention back into the 90%+ range, and positive EBIT from early 2026 as revenue scales ahead of operating costs. These outcomes are contingent on rebuilding new-logo volume and stabilising retention, particularly in weaker segments and geographies identified in the actuals.

  • Retention and expansion quality: Actual gross and net retention trended below healthy SaaS ranges and drove Q4’25 deceleration. Typical levers: root-cause churn analysis by segment/region, proactive save playbooks for at-risk cohorts, packaging/pricing to protect ARR, and CS capacity alignment to high-risk accounts.
  • New logo engine resilience: Actual Q4’25 new logos declined (8 in the quarter) and deal value slowed. Typical levers: pipeline coverage/aging audits, win-loss by segment, demand-mix rebalancing, and conversion-path fixes (discovery → proposal → close).
  • Operating leverage to profitability: EBIT remains slightly negative on actuals; the forecast expects break-even and expansion in 2026. Typical levers: guardrails on G&A (which ran above budget), consistent S&M efficiency at current CAC/payback, and fit-for-purpose hiring pacing versus ARR per head.
page1:
The dashboard shows a scaled but mixed health profile on actuals through December 2025. Strengths: ARR £9.4M with 70% growth, gross margin 78% and recurring margin 83%, CAC ratio ~0.56 and LTV/CAC 6.5 supporting efficient customer acquisition, and Rule of 40 at 63 indicating acceptable balance of growth and profitability. Constraints: retention metrics are below robust SaaS norms (logo 85%, gross 79%, net 90%), and EBIT margin at -7% confirms the P&L has not yet reached break-even.

Beyond December 2025, any upward trends are forecast and should be viewed as expectations rather than achieved outcomes.

  • Management focus reinforced: Rebuild retention to >90% gross and >100% net by prioritising save motions, onboarding quality, and expansion playbooks; maintain acquisition efficiency while lifting new-logo volume to avoid repeating Q4’25 deceleration.
page2:
Actual ARR rose from £6.84M (Mar’25) to £9.42M (Dec’25), but momentum softened in Q4’25: ARR net add was £0.51M versus £0.86–£1.31M in prior quarters. Actual logo retention fell to 84% in Dec’25, and new logos declined to 8, both contributing to slower net growth. Net retention for the Dec’25 quarter printed at 91%.

The forecast assumes a recovery: logo retention moves back into the 90s and ARR grows to £17.6M by Dec’27, implying sustained quarterly net adds and improved deal flow. These are projections, not achieved results.

  • Management focus sharpened: Stabilise churn and reignite new-logo intake. Actions typically include (1) pipeline quality and coverage diagnostics by segment/region, (2) renewal risk scoring and save motions 120–180 days out, and (3) pricing/packaging guardrails to reduce downsell while enabling expansion.
page3:
On actuals through Q4’25, revenue expanded each quarter (£1.69M → £2.61M). Gross margin held ~78–79%. Operating costs grew modestly; EBIT improved from -£0.36M in Q1’25 to -£0.05M in Q4’25, indicating emerging leverage but not yet break-even. Mix-wise, S&M percentage declined over the year, while G&A remained meaningful. Headcount scaled from 53 to 64.

The forecast projects positive EBIT from early 2026 and continued headcount growth to 106 by Dec’27. Realisation of this path depends on delivering the forecasted ARR growth and maintaining margin discipline.

  • Management focus reinforced: Protect gross margin while enforcing G&A discipline (given budget variance) and pacing hiring to ARR per head, ensuring the shift to sustained positive EBIT does not rely solely on optimistic top-line assumptions.
page4:
Actual ARR composition to Dec’25 is concentrated in Energy & Utilities and Life Sciences. Retention signals by segment are mixed: Finance & Services shows materially weak net retention (≈44%), while Energy & Utilities and Life Sciences are at or above 100% on a 12‑month basis. By geography, North America underperforms on net retention (~88%) versus other regions in the low-to-mid 90s. The rolling NRR line dipped to ~90% in late 2025 before a modest uptick to ~92% in December.

Any improvement beyond December is forecast. The concentration and underperforming cohorts identified in the actuals warrant targeted action to prevent further drag on net growth.

  • Management focus sharpened: Segment-specific retention plans—tighten ICP and success motions in Finance & Services and North America; align product/enablement to the needs driving churn, and rebalance go-to-market emphasis toward segments with ≥100% NRR while remediation is underway.
page5:
Signals from the last 3 months show a December-led spike in new-logo ARR, modest expansions, and a small downsell in November. Only November and December 2025 are actuals; January 2026 entries are part of the forecast and should not be interpreted as realized transactions. The actual mix skews toward new lands rather than expansions, consistent with the broader retention/NRR softness.

These short-term movements corroborate the Q4’25 slowdown despite a solid December landing month, reinforcing the need to strengthen renewals and expansion quality alongside new-logo intake.

No new management focus items identified on this page.
page6:
Versus the 2025 budget, actuals delivered a modest revenue beat (+1%) and slightly lower gross profit (-1%), with EBITDA better by £30k (+5%). Departmentally, S&M and Development underspent relative to budget (favorable), while G&A overspent materially (unfavorable). ARR finished 11% above the annual budget, driven primarily by stronger additions and lower-than-budgeted attrition; downsell and upsell underperformed plan.

Quarterly and monthly views for Q4 show consistent outperformance on EBITDA versus budget, indicating disciplined execution late in the year. The forecast assumes these trends continue; realization depends on retention improvement and controlled overhead growth.

  • Management focus reinforced: Tighten G&A controls to eliminate leakage while protecting S&M efficiency; ensure 2026 plan risk-adjusts for the observed downsell/upsell shortfalls and allocates capacity to renewal saves and expansion plays.
